main_deity: A replica of the Svayambhū Caitya (as digudyaḥ)
description_en: Ituṃ Bāhāḥ Nani is an elongated courtyard with a god house (dyaḥchẽ) of the patron deity (digudyaḥ) of the members of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ, and severalcaityas. The courtyard is known as Aśoka Maṇḍapa Vihāra in Sanskrit (Locke 1985, p.290; R. Vajrācārya & V. Vajrācārya 1103, p.24). Despite having the characteristics of anani,* locals refer to it as Ituṃ Bāhāḥ instead. However, the actual Ituṃ Bāhāḥ (KAT1220) is located in an adjacent courtyard west of the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ Nani. Locke (1985, p.290) incorrectly referred to this Nani as Kāygu Nani. According to locals, Kāygu Nani is a nearby courtyard. Thedigudyaḥ, represented by a replica of the Svayaṃbhū Caitya, of the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ members is enshrined on the first floor of the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ Nani’s north-facing three-storydyaḥchẽ. It has a veranda on the second floor. After worshipping theirdigudyaḥ, the members of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ use the second floor to host feasts. The members of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ are said to have moved here from Sankhu and thus revere the Svayambhū Caitya established inside Jogeśvara Mandira/Gũ Bāhāḥ (SKH0510) as theirdigudyaḥ. Therefore, a replica of the Svayambhū Caitya is housed in the sanctum of the Nani'sdyaḥchẽ.Statues of other tantric deities like Māricī are also enshrined inside the sanctum of thedyaḥchẽ(based on private communication with a local resident, Śākya, male, age 62). Only members of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ are permitted to enter thedyaḥchẽ. The door on the ground floor has a woodentoraṇawith an image of Mahāvairocana at the centre. In the Nani courtyard, 15caityashave been erected.The Nani's first historical record is an inscription from 1641 CE (NS 762) recording the installation of a pair of lions in front of the main entrance to thedyaḥchẽ. Another inscription from 1654 CE (NS 774) states that three people, including Narasiṃhadeva, built a structure fordigudyaḥ. This suggests thatdigudyaḥwas originally an open shrine, and thedyaḥchẽwas constructed only in 1654 CE.Except for the Vajradhātu Caitya (object no. KAT1200-010) in front of the entrance to the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ's courtyard,** all of the caityas at the Nani are from the Śāha period (after the 18thcentury). The Nani'sdyaḥchẽwas rebuilt in 2021 CE (VS 2077) with funds provided by the Hanumandhoka Palace Area Conservation Program.Pruscha (1975, vol. II, p. 44 (C/K-120)) describes the Nani as follows: “This is among the oldest and most important monasteries in Kathmandu. Its earliest date is the fourteenth century when Madana Ram consecrated an image of Dipankara, and his wife consecrated a golden image of Aryatara here. Although the shrine’s façade is quite ordinary, its elaborately carved wooden torana, which represents Mahavairochana Buddha, is an outstanding work. The short struts show the Buddha Chaturakarsini. There are a number of chaityas in the courtyard. The famous demon of the town Gurumapa is connected with this bahal. The monastery is also linked with the bathing ceremony of the Red Machchendranath of Patan.”* Ananiis a large courtyard enclosed on all four sides by private buildings but may also include a monastery on one side.** The elders of the Iṭuṃ Bāhāḥ had renovated this Caitya in 1668 CE.
description_ne: इतुं बाहाः ननिको दक्षिणमा इतुं बाहाःका संघ-सदस्यहरूको दिगुद्यः राखिएको द्यःछेँ रहेको छ । नेसं ७७४ (सन् १६५४) मा निर्माण गरिएको यस द्यःछेँको पेटीमा राखेर कङ्गः अजिमालाई सगुन दिने परम्परा छ ।काठमाडौंको इतुं बाहाः (KAT1220) भित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकाबाहिर रहेको खुल्ला ठाउँ नै इतुं बाहाः ननि हो । यसलाई ननि भनिएपनि वास्तवमा यो एउटा विहार नै हो । संस्कृतमा यसलाई अशोक मण्डप विहार भनिएको छ (Locke1985, p.290;R. Vajrācārya & V. Vajrācārya1103, p.24) । स्थानीयहरू यसलाई ननि भन्दैनन्, 'इतुं बाहाः' नै भन्छन् । क्वाःपाःद्यः स्थापना गरिएको पारावर्त महाविहारलाई चाहिँ 'बाहाः दुने' भन्ने गर्छन् ।Locke(1985, p.290) ले यसलाई 'कायगु ननि' लेखेका छन्, तर स्थानीयका अनुसार यसको नाम कायगु ननि होइन । कायगु ननि चाहिँ इतुं बाहाःबाट नरदेवी जाने गल्लीमा रहेको छ । इतुं बाहाः ननिको दक्षिणमा इतुं बाहाःका संघ-सदस्यहरूको दिगुद्यः स्थापना गरिएको द्यःछेँ रहेको छ । तीन तलाको उत्तराभिमुख उक्त द्यःछेँको दोस्रो तलामा बार्दली निकालिएको छ । यस तलामा इतुं बाहाःका संघ-सदस्यहरू जम्मा भई दिगुद्यः पूजा गरी भोज खाने गरिन्छ । द्यःछेँको पहिलो तलामा पासुखाझ्याः राखिएको छ । यस तलामा इतुं बाहाःका संघ-सदस्यहरूको दिगुद्यः स्थापना गरिएको छ । क्वाःपाःद्यः नभई इतुं बाहाःका संघ-सदस्यहरूको दिगुद्यः स्थापना गरिएको छ । इतुं बाहाःका मानिसहरू साँखुको वज्रयोगिनीबाट बसाइँ सरेर आएका थिए । त्यसैले उनीहरू साँखुको जोगेश्वर मन्दिर / गुँ बाहाः (SKH0510) भित्र रहेको स्वयम्भू चैत्यलाई दिगुद्यःको रूपमा मान्छन् । त्यसै स्वयम्भू चैत्यको प्रतिकृतिलाई द्यःछेँको पहिलो तलामा स्थापना गरिएको छ । मारिची लगायत अन्य तान्त्रिक देवीदेवताहरू पनि स्थापना गरिएका छन् (केशचन्द्र महाविहार संरक्षण समाजका अध्यक्ष, शाक्य थरका, वर्ष ६२ सँगको कुराकानीमा आधारित) ।[1]द्यःछेँको भुइँतला खाली नै रहेको छ । द्यःछेँभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामाथि महावैरोचन अङ्कित काष्ठतोरण राखिएको छ । ननिमा १५ वटा चैत्य स्थापना गरिएका छन् ।यस ननिमा प्राप्त सबभन्दा पुरानो ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण नेसं ७६२ (सन् १६४१) को अभिलेख हो । उक्त अभिलेखमा इतुं बाहाःका कुनै आःजुका छोराहरू जक्ष र सिंह दुईजनाले मिलेर दिगुद्यःछेँको प्रवेशद्वार अगाडि एक जोडी ढुङ्गाको सिंह स्थापना गरेको कुरा लेखिएको छ । नेसं ७७४ (सन् १६५४) मा नरसिंहदेव सहित तीनजनाले मिलेर दिगुद्यःको लागि प्रासाद (भवन) बनाइदिएका थिए । पहिले खुल्ला ठाउँमा रहेको दिगुद्यःलाई पछि घर बनाएर विधिपूर्वक स्थापना गरेको हुनुपर्छ । राजा प्रताप मल्लको राज्यकालमा नेसं ७८८ (सन् १६६८) मा इतुं बाहाःका आःजुहरूले मिलेर इतुं बाहाःभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोका बाहिर रहेको वज्रधातु चैत्य जीर्णोद्धार गरेका थिए । ननिमा रहेका अन्य चैत्यहरू धेरै पछि शाहकालमा मात्र स्थापना गरिएका हुन् । विसं २०७७ (सन् २०२१) मा काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाको हनुमानढोका राजदरवार क्षेत्र संरक्षण कार्यक्रम मार्फत् प्राप्त आर्थिक सहयोगबाट दिगुद्यः राखिएको द्यःछेँको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।ननिमा रहेको दिगुद्यःको द्यःछेँमा इतुं बाहाःका चक्रेश्वरले मात्र नित्यपूजा गर्छन् । पहिले बाहाःका १० जना आःजुहरूले एक-एक महिनाको पालो मिलाएर द्यःछेँमा नित्यपूजा गर्थे (N. Śarmā2005, p.138, p.25) । इतुं बाहाःको संघमा १० वटा खलकका मानिसहरू आवद्ध छन् । ती १० वटा खलकले वैशाख शुक्ल ३ (अक्षय तृतीया) देखि ज्येष्ठ शुक्ल ६ (सिथिनखः) भित्रमा आ-आफ्नो तिथिअनुसार द्यःछेँमा दिगुपूजा मनाउँछन् । कङ्गः अजिमा (KAT1010) जात्राको क्रममा प्रत्येक वर्ष चैत्र कृष्ण औंसीमा देवीको खटलाई इतुं बाहाःमा ल्याई दिगुद्यःको द्यःछेँको पेटीमा राखी बाहाःका आःजुहरूले सगुन दिने परम्परा छ । ननिको क्षेत्रफल ठूलो भएकोले कुनै सभासम्मेलन वा कुनै धार्मिक-सांस्कृतिक गतिविधि (सामूहिक इही, वसुन्धरा व्रत) गर्नुपरेमा पनि यस ननिलाई प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।Footnotes^द्यःछेँभित्र इतुं बाहाःका संघ-सदस्यहरू बाहेक अरूलाई प्रवेश निषेध गरिएकोले दिगुद्यःको फोटो खिच्न सकिँदैन ।

historical_events.event_name: Installation of a pair of lions
historical_events.event_description: Jakṣa and Siṃha, sons of one of the elders of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ, erected the pair of stone lions in front of the entrance of thedyaḥchẽ.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of a dyaḥchẽ for lineage deity
historical_events.event_description: According to the stone inscription from NS 774 (1654 CE) affixed to the backside of thedyaḥchẽ, three people, including Narasiṃhadeva, built a god house (dyaḥchẽ) fordigudyaḥ. This suggests thatdigudyaḥwas initially an open shrine, and thedyaḥchẽwas constructed only in 1654 CE.

historical_events.event_name: Renovation of the Vajradhātu Caitya (object no. KAT1200-010)
historical_events.event_description: During the reign of King Pratāpa Malla, the elders of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ renovated the Caitya in front of the entrance to the courtyard of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Pañcāvaliyukta Caitya (object no. KAT1200-015)
historical_events.event_description: During the reign of King Rājendra Vikrama Śāha, Bhājuvīra Śākyabhikṣu (text: Sākebhikṣu Bhājubila) constructed the Caitya in memory of his father Bekhāsiṃhadeva (text: Bekhāsiṃdeo). He also endowed some plots of land to make periodic offerings (śrāddha) to six of his ancestors and perform the anniversary ritual of the Caitya.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Jalaharyoparijinālaṅkṛta Caitya (object no. KAT1200-014)
historical_events.event_description: Together with his family, Dharmasiṃha (text: Dharmmasiṃha) constructed the Caitya at the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ Nani.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Jalaharyoparijinālaṅkṛta Caitya (object no. KAT1200-011)
historical_events.event_description: Śākyabhikṣu Jujuvirasiṃ constructed the Caitya in memory of his father Dhirjavīrasiṃ.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (object no. KAT1200-008)
historical_events.event_description: Devalakṣmī Maharjana, Hela Thakuṃ, and Pune Thakuṃ of the Yatkhā Ṭola constructed the Caitya at the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ Nani. They also endowed some plots of land to observe the anniversary ritual of the Caitya.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (object no. KAT1200-017)
historical_events.event_description: Jīvaratna constructed the Caitya (KAT1200-017) at the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ Nani in memory of Dhirjamāna of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (object no. KAT1200-007)
historical_events.event_description: During the reign of King Vīrendra Śāha, Jogaratna (an elder 'āḥju'of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ) constructed the Caitya at the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ Nani.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (object no. KAT1200-016)
historical_events.event_description: Dharmasiṃha constructed the Caitya at the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ Nani in memory of his father Dhanavīra (text: Dhanabi).

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (object no. KAT1200-006)
historical_events.event_description: Jogaratna Śākya (an elder 'āḥju'of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ) constructed the Caitya at the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ Nani.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (object no. KAT1200-013)
historical_events.event_description: Najaramāna and his family constructed the Caitya at the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ Nani in memory of Caturamāna.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (object no. KAT1200-018)
historical_events.event_description: Members of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ constructed the Caitya.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (object no. KAT1200-019)
historical_events.event_description: Cinīkumārī Śākya and her family constructed the Caitya in memory of Sānu Śākya, an elder 'āḥju' of Ituṃ Bāhāḥ.
Thedyaḥchẽwas reconstructed with funds provided by the Kathmandu Metropolitan City Office's Hanumandhoka Palace Area Conservation Program.
